newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: EU says Israel must show commitment to peace.
newsitem.headline: EU says Israel must show commitment to peace.

text.p: The European Union criticised Israel on Thursday over the crisis with the Palestinians, calling on it to avoid actions that could be seen as provocative and to show it was committed to peace.

Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, who speaks for the 15-nation bloc because his country now holds the EU presidency, made the remarks at a news conference on the margins of the U.N. General Assembly in New York.
Israeli and Palestinian forces fought gunbattles in the West Bank and Gaza on Thursday. About 40 Palestinians and at least 10 Israelis have been killed in two days of clashes.

EU foreign ministers discussed the latest Middle East crisis with U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher on Wednesday and Spring said he had also talked with Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy. Spring said the EU had conveyed to Levy "our deepest concern in relation to the lack of momentum in the peace process."

"We emphasised very strongly and affirmatively the concern of the European Union that it was necessary for Israel to show ... a renewed commitment to the process ... signals need to be given by the Israeli government," Spring said.

He said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu should maintain contacts with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to show the world that Israel will honour peace agreements reached by the previous Israeli government.

Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said the U.N. Security Council would discuss the Middle East as part of regular consultations later on Thursday and that European countries wanted to send a clear message to Israel.
"It is necessary for Israel to give a signal, to take action that will demonstrate ... that Israel remains committed to peace. We need some steps that go in the right direction," Dini told reporters.

"The disturbing fact ... is that in the Arab countries in the region the credibility of the Israeli government is being questioned and its commitment to peace, and that, I think, is dangerous and should not be allowed to continue."

Arab anger at Netanyahu's failure to extend self-rule in the West Bank and Gaza boiled over after his Likud government opened a tunnel near the al-Aqsa and Dome of the Rock mosques, sites holy to Islam.

"Matters like that should be avoided in a situation which is particularly tense and fragile. ... Great care should be taken in terms of any action that could cause incidents and loss of life," Spring said.
